Leaf blades elliptic, flat, membranous, 1.5 – 6 × 0.5 – 1 cm, drying yellow-green, glabrous or with sparse bulbous-based cilia on both sides. Panicles terminal, partly or fully exserted on a peduncle 5 – 7 cm long, 4 – 10 cm long, ovate, side branches single, the branches divergent at maturity, scabrous, the spikelets usually paired

children.name: Chusquea anelythra Nees
children.description: Etymology: — According to McClure & Smith (1967), the specific epithet “ anelythra ” has a Greek origin and means an = “ without ” and elytra = “ coverage or scale ”, referring to the very reduced lower pair of glumes of this species. Habitat and distribution: — Chusquea anelythra is endemic to Brazil, occurring in montane forests and Atlantic forest fragments of Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais, Espírito Santo, and Bahia, along rivers and streams at 860 ‒ 1450 m. a. s. l. (Table 1, Figs. 3 and 4).

children.description: Phenology: — Three collections in flower were found among the studied specimens, from 1972, 2003, and 2007. Assuming that the 2003 and 2007 collections (Lombardi 5505 & Viana 3183, respectively) represent a gregarious flowering event, as does Soderstrom’s type collection, in 1972, we suggest a possible flowering cycle of 31 to 35 years. However, as only a few flowering collections are known, these figures are merely speculative.
